pulse: Equities rallied broadly: the S&P 500 rose 2.35% to 7549.94, the Nasdaq 100 jumped 3.40% to 27907.63, the Dow added 2.15% to 52389.75, and the Russell 2000 gained 3.15% to 2840.81, with breadth firmly positive at 423 advancers vs 78 decliners. Producer Manufacturing was the strongest sector (+6.10%, led by AMAT +11.37% and LRCX +10.41%), while Energy Minerals was the laggard, barely positive at +0.06% as XOM (-0.69%) and CVX (-0.86%) slipped. Risk appetite was evident off the tape too: the VIX collapsed 22.31% to 19.92, the 10Y yield eased 0.37% to 4.87%, the dollar (DXY) softened 0.05% to 101.62, and WTI crude fell 1.26% to $85.76, while gold slipped 0.35% and Bitcoin dropped 0.88%. Among the most-active names, NVDA was the standout decliner at -4.27% on a massive 462.72M shares ($82.67B traded) even as chip peers AMD (+13.26%) and MU (+6.25%) surged, while FRVO (+26.09%) and WBHC (-47.09%) topped the broader gainers and losers lists.
